blocks.text: CSS Media Queries
CSS Media Queries

CSS media queries allow you to apply styles based on the characteristics of a
device or the environment displaying the web page.
CSS media queries are essential for creating responsive web pages.

The CSS @media rule
is used to add media queries to your style sheet.
Media Query Syntax

A media query consists of an optional media-type and one or more
media-features, which resolve to either true or false.
The media-type is optional. However, if you use not, you must also specify a media-type.

The result of a media query is true if the specified media-type matches the type of device, and all media-features are true. When a media query is true, the corresponding style rules are
applied, following the normal cascading rules.
Meaning of the not and and keywords:
not: This optional keyword inverts the meaning of the entire media query.

and: This keyword combines a media-type and one or more
media-features.
CSS Media Types

The optional media type specifies the type of media the styles are for. If
media type is omitted, it will be set to "all".

rows: Used for all media type devices
Used for computer screens, tablets, and smart-phones

blocks.text: CSS Media Features
The media feature specifies a specific characteristic of the device.
Here are some commonly used media features:

rows: Orientation of the viewport (landscape or portrait)
User's preferred color scheme (light or dark)
